pharm: Symptomatic slow-acting drug for osteoarthritis (SYSADOA) / supplement
quick: 1500 mg glucosamine sulfate once daily (KCl-stabilized salt)
Take with or after meals to reduce GI upset
Caution; potassium load from KCl salt in severe impairment
Caution; limited data in severe impairment
Glycemic control in diabetics, INR if on warfarin, symptom response
summary: Glucosamine sulfate potassium chloride is a potassium-chloride-stabilized salt of glucosamine sulfate used as a symptomatic slow-acting drug (SYSADOA) for mild-to-moderate knee osteoarthritis. The standard dose delivers 1500 mg of glucosamine sulfate once daily. It is not FDA-approved (sold as a supplement in the US; a prescription product in parts of Europe/Asia). Onset of symptomatic benefit is gradual over weeks. It is generally well tolerated; cautions include shellfish allergy, the added potassium load, and glycemic/INR effects.
indications: Relief of symptoms (pain and functional impairment) in mild to moderate osteoarthritis, especially of the knee
Slowing of symptomatic progression of osteoarthritis (where approved as a SYSADOA)

dosage.d: Equivalent to 1500 mg glucosamine sulfate once daily (KCl-stabilized)
dosage.n: May divide into 500 mg three times daily
Stop if no benefit after 2-3 months

dosage.d: No specific dosing established; use cautiously
dosage.n: Consider potassium load from KCl salt in renal impairment

admin: Take orally once daily, preferably with or after meals to minimize GI upset
Dissolve sachet/powder formulations fully in water before drinking if applicable
Allow several weeks of continuous use to judge symptomatic benefit
Reassess at 2-3 months and discontinue if there is no response
moa: Glucosamine is an aminomonosaccharide and natural substrate for synthesis of glycosaminoglycans and proteoglycans in articular cartilage. Exogenous glucosamine sulfate is proposed to stimulate cartilage matrix synthesis and inhibit catabolic/inflammatory enzymes (e.g., aggrecanase, IL-1-mediated effects), exerting a slow symptomatic and possible structure-modifying effect in osteoarthritis. The potassium chloride stabilizes the otherwise hygroscopic glucosamine sulfate salt.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to glucosamine or formulation components
Allergy to shellfish (most glucosamine is shellfish-derived)
relative: Diabetes mellitus / impaired glucose tolerance (monitor glycemia)
Severe renal impairment (potassium load from KCl)

preg: There are insufficient data on the safety of glucosamine in pregnancy. Use is not recommended during pregnancy.
lact: There are insufficient data on excretion in breast milk and infant safety. Use is not recommended during breastfeeding.
renal: Limited data in renal impairment; the potassium chloride content may contribute to potassium load, so use with caution and monitor in moderate-to-severe impairment.
hepatic: Limited data in hepatic impairment; use with caution as safety has not been established.

major: Warfarin - case reports of increased INR and bleeding risk; monitor INR closely
moderate: Antidiabetic agents - glucosamine may affect glucose control; monitor blood glucose
Other potassium-raising drugs - additive potassium with the KCl component in renal impairment
minor: Tetracyclines - theoretical increased absorption; chemotherapy (etoposide, doxorubicin) - theoretical reduced effect
interactions.food: Take with food; no specific food to avoid.
interactions.diagnostics: May alter blood glucose readings; can prolong INR in patients on warfarin; KCl salt may raise serum potassium.

monitoring: Symptom and functional response over 2-3 months
Blood glucose in patients with diabetes or glucose intolerance
Signs of allergic reaction in shellfish-sensitive patients
counsel: This may take several weeks to relieve joint symptoms; do not expect immediate relief
Tell your doctor if you are allergic to shellfish before starting
If you have diabetes, check your blood sugar more often when starting
If you take warfarin, your INR will need monitoring
Stop if there is no benefit after about 2-3 months and discuss alternatives
pk: Gradual symptomatic effect over 2-4 weeks or longer
Plasma glucosamine peak ~3-4 hours after oral dose
Supports once-daily dosing; benefit may persist after stopping
Store in a cool, dry place protected from moisture
pearls: NOT FDA-approved - marketed as a dietary supplement in the US; a prescription SYSADOA in parts of Europe/Asia. This record is based on EMA/SmPC and BNF/monograph data, not an FDA label
The potassium chloride salt stabilizes hygroscopic glucosamine sulfate - account for the small added potassium load in renal impairment
Most glucosamine is derived from shellfish - avoid in shellfish allergy
Monitor blood glucose in diabetics and INR in warfarin users
Crystalline glucosamine sulfate (1500 mg once daily) is the best-studied formulation; effect is slow and modest
missed: If you miss a dose, take it when you remember unless it is nearly time for the next dose, in which case skip the missed dose. Do not double up. Consistent daily use over weeks is what matters for benefit.
overdose: Overdose experience is limited; high intake may cause gastrointestinal upset, headache and, with the potassium chloride salt, potential potassium elevation in renal impairment. Management is supportive with monitoring of potassium and glucose as appropriate.
